body:
Dropping (striking) a receiving container removes its declaration; the channel pools'
inboxOf edges then dangle, subtreeOf's fixpoint reaches nothing, and the dashboard renders
its scope-honest empty state — while channelStatus still lists the channels receiving:true
and any resumed sync keeps writing peer bytes to disk (T203's erasure lens, 2026-08-21;
admin.ts ~144-162, admin-pages.ts reach filter). The channels are ownerless: no page shows
them, no subtree reaches them, and they keep pulling.

CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES THE DESIGN: the frozen T203 rail
(test/server/admin-channel-health.test.ts, test (c)) pins that POST /admin/drop on a
container that channels feed returns 200 and renders the confirm page with the honesty note.
So this ticket does NOT add a refusal — refusing the strike is a lifecycle-semantics change
that belongs with T214's pool-seam design (they decide together what a channel's relationship
to its container's lifecycle IS, and that is Myk's ground). This ticket makes the orphan
state VISIBLE, which no frozen rail constrains:

Build: an orphaned-channels block. A channel whose `into` container no longer resolves in the
container table renders on the dashboard of every user with the operator role (gate by
rolesOf(gw.reactor, gw.operatorAuthor, user).has("operator") — the postRegister precedent in
admin.ts ~1000; non-operator users see nothing, because the orphans are outside every
subtree by construction and reach-scoping is the page's contract). Each row names the channel,
its health (the T203 renderer), and the verbs that resolve it (`loam federate drop` /
`federate set --receiving false`). `loam federate list` already sees orphans; add the
"orphaned — its receiving container is gone" marker there too.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A store with an orphaned channel (fixture: open channel, strike the receiving container
    through the real confirm flow) shows the orphaned block on an operator-role user's
    dashboard, naming the channel and its verbs; a non-operator user's dashboard shows
    nothing (two-sided). Verify: new test test/server/admin-orphan-channels.test.ts with the
    session fixture.
(b) `loam federate list` marks the orphan; a healthy channel carries no marker (two-sided).
    Verify: new test in test/cli/ (drop-cli.test.ts is frozen).
(c) The existing confirm-page flow is byte-unchanged (the frozen T203 rail stays green
    untouched). Verify: the frozen rail itself plus rails-guard-ci.

Merge tier: repair — visibility of a state the store already permits. Self-merge on the
ordinary bar. Whether striking should REFUSE while channels feed the container is recorded as
an open question on T214's design ground, not decided here.
title: Striking a receiving container orphans its channels — make the orphans visible
